general_findings: Reduced smoke opacity meaningfully restores dense-scene readability compared with opaque craggy-puff variants; impacts remain recognizable.
Tall structures and aircraft shadows retain convincing height cues; base apron and vegetation grouping improve terrain structure.
Directional ocean streaks look stretched or motion-blurred rather than like layered water. This loses natural material variation despite lower visual clutter.
Black shoreline strips resemble seams or exposed geometry against the sand; their intended physical meaning is unclear.
Historical circle particles and rectangular wakes are particularly weak in physical coherence and obscure combat.
regressions: Long regular ocean bands reduce natural water richness.
Dark shoreline strips interrupt beach without convincing transition.
Repeated separated wake puffs remain artificial.
Dense fire specks and duplicate aircraft shadows still compete with the player.
recommendations: Keep restrained smoke, hot impact cores, raised structures and functional apron.
Restore multidirectional small water variation while keeping low contrast; avoid uniformly long stripes.
Resolve shore strips into deliberate continuous material with contact shading, or remove the seam-like segments.
Make player silhouette survive deck overlap and reduce effect density locally around it.
